html:
The main stock exchange of the United States, on Wall Street in New York City, and the largest in the world by the value of the companies it lists.

It traces its start to the Buttonwood Agreement of 17 May 1792, when 24 brokers met, by tradition under a buttonwood tree on Wall Street, and agreed to trade only with one another at fixed fees. At first they dealt mostly in the government bonds that Alexander Hamilton had issued to pay off the debts of the Revolution, and in bank shares such as those of the Bank of North America.

In 1817 the brokers formed a formal board with written rules. New York's rise as a port after the Erie Canal helped make its exchange the nation's financial centre. Railroads, then industrial giants, raised money on it.

Its worst days are part of world history. The crash of 1929 opened the Great Depression, and the 2008 financial crisis shook markets everywhere.
sum: The main stock exchange of the United States, on Wall Street in New York City, and the largest in the world by the value of the companies it lists.
